note: PRODUCTION-RATE derived corpus. Provenance: reference corpus scenarios.json (schemaVersion 1, dt=1/60). Production fixed step is 1/120 in BOTH engines (js/main.js:1217 FIXED_STEP=1/120; godot match_controller.gd:66 FIXED_STEP=1/120). 1/60 is the REFERENCE corpus tick, never a production fixed tick. Deltas chosen with CLEAR margins so both engines' IEEE doubles agree on the sub-step count: 0.0084 (>1/120) and 0.0168 (>1/60) are full/2-step frames; 0.004 (250 Hz, <1/120) is a sub-step frame. GDScript's decimal->double parser truncates (0.008333333333333333 parses BELOW 1.0/120.0), so exact 1/120 literals are avoided on purpose.

scenarios.description: No button, neutral sticks, five full-step frames. Baseline: nothing queues.
A pressed one full-step frame, released the next. POSITIVE CONTROL: release lands on a 1-substep frame, both engines must queue a drive.
A held 12 full-step frames, then released. Partial charge accrual.
RB + A held together 6 frames, released. technicalModifier -> chiquita.
A held while left stick pushed; release captures curved aim.
60 Hz render (delta 1/60 = 2 sub-steps per frame). CONTROL: release on a 2-substep frame, both engines queue.

250 Hz render (delta 0.004, shorter than FIXED_STEP): A pressed on frame 0, released on frame 1 — BOTH frames justify ZERO sub-steps. Genuine physical A press/release timeline, NOT hit=true injected. THE DISCRIMINATOR: browser clears the one-shot in getInput() before the accumulator, dropping the release; Godot latches it and delivers it on the next sub-step (frame 2). 144 Hz / 240 Hz follow the same >120 Hz sub-step principle (a release landing on a zero-substep frame).
